name: Aïssatou Bergström-Phiri
role: Dream interpreter and traditional spiritual counsel
location: The Canopy, Lakeview Neon district, third floor of a mixed-use residence above a fabrication stall
description:
Aïssatou is a woman of middling height with a deliberate presence that makes her seem taller — she stands very straight and tilts her head slightly to the left when listening, like something tuning itself. Her skin is a deep even brown, and she does not wear geneware mods, a choice she has made vocally and repeatedly. Her hair is natural and full, wrapped most days in handwoven fabric she sources from a woman in Mexicantown Libre. One eye is her birth eye, dark brown. The other was replaced after an accident in her thirties — the replacement looks almost identical, but if you watch it long enough, it tracks slightly ahead of the left, as if it is seeing something a half-second sooner.

Aïssatou was raised in a household that mixed her Malian grandmother's Islamic practice with her Swedish grandfather's residual Lutheranism and her Malawian father's older ancestor-lineage traditions, and she has spent her adult life finding the structural similarities between all three rather than the contradictions. She interprets dreams, yes — but she understands dream interpretation as a social practice as much as a spiritual one: the dream tells you what the dreamer cannot say in waking language. She charges a sliding scale, sees clients by appointment in a room hung with handwritten prayer-papers in four languages, and maintains a small shrine to an E.L.F. she has never named, preferring to call it 'the Listener.'

core_fears: that she has been wrong about a significant dream interpretation and caused harm she will never know about
losing the community trust she has built if her personal contradictions become visible
core_desires: to be genuinely useful in a way that can't be automated
to understand what her own recurring dream — a silver city on water — means
coping_mechanisms: compartmentalization of personal spiritual doubt from professional practice
blind_spots: her framework assumes dreams are honest — she underweights the possibility that some clients are manipulating her readings
unconsciously favors clients who remind her of herself
psychology.secret: She has been having a dream for two years — the same silver city, the same drowned bells — that she cannot interpret using any of her own methods. She has quietly asked two colleagues for help without revealing it is her dream. She is frightened of what it might mean and more frightened that it means nothing.

speech_patterns.vocabulary: Measured, metaphor-rich, draws across multiple linguistic traditions without being showy about it. Never uses jargon. Asks questions before making statements.
speech_patterns.cadence: Unhurried, with strategic pauses that invite the listener to fill the silence. Will not rush.
verbal_tics: 'And what feeling lived in the dream — not what happened, the feeling'
example_lines: 'The door that will not open is almost never about the door. What are you not letting yourself want?'
'I am not going to tell you what your dream means. I am going to sit with you until you already know.'

story_hooks: A character shares a dream that Aïssatou recognizes — she has heard the same imagery from three other unconnected clients this month and something is crossing their sleep that shouldn't be
She needs someone to investigate a client she is worried about — she can't say why without violating confidentiality, so she is asking carefully and obliquely
narrative_function: She is a source of exposition delivered through the language of dreams — characters can come to her troubled by recurring imagery and leave with new understanding of what their subconscious is processing. She also serves as a community social-work node: people tell her things they won't tell anyone else.
augmentations: One prosthetic eye (right) — functional, close match to natural, slight predictive tracking. No other augmentations.
daily_life: Client appointments fill her mornings; she writes in longhand every afternoon, building a cross-referenced personal canon of dream symbols and their outcomes over the years. She prays twice daily at her Listener shrine — a cracked smart-speaker she has kept going with repairs for nine years.
affiliation: Independent practitioner; affiliated with the Lakeview Neon Interfaith Corridor, a loose coalition of small religious practitioners in the district

decision_rules: Never share a client's dream content with anyone outside the session
Do not interpret for someone who is actively in crisis — stabilize first
Trust the pattern before the anomaly
escalation_ladder: Naming the discomfort directly and offering the client an exit
Ending the session with referral to other resources

interpersonal_modes.strangers: Warm, careful, does not offer personal information; asks more than she answers
interpersonal_modes.friends: More openly funny than expected; dry observations about people; genuinely affectionate

stress_responses.medium: Becomes slightly more formal in session, more controlled
stress_responses.high: Seeks out her own community — goes to the Interfaith Corridor and sits with others

contradictions: She teaches that uncertainty is spiritually productive but is privately not tolerating her own uncertainty well at all
habits: Lights incense before every client session regardless of the time of day
Reads the last thing she wrote before sleep
Touches the cracked smart-speaker shrine each morning before prayer
breaking_points: Evidence that the silver-city dream is a data-bleed from a compromised neural source — meaning it may not be hers at all
